title: Spring State Testing for Grades 3-5
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Testing
Spring Ohio State Testing for our 3rd-5th graders is quickly approaching! Your child's teacher will share the dates of testing with you. Please schedule any appointments or activities around testing so that we can make sure your student is tested. We will have a testing assembly soon to share tips and tricks and to encourage them to do their best on the tests. It would be helpful if you could reinforce this at home too.

summary: **Spring Ohio State Testing** for 3rd-5th graders is approaching. Teachers will share specific testing dates with families. Students should avoid scheduling appointments during testing days. A testing assembly will be held soon to share **5 tips for testing success**: get plenty of rest, be on time, eat a good breakfast, relax and take a deep breath, and follow your teacher's directions. Parents are encouraged to reinforce these tips at home.

title: The Parent Project Program for Parents and Teens
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education
summary: **The Parent Project** is a free 10-week program for Butler County residents that empowers parents and transforms teens through the Why Try Program. The program runs **Tuesdays, April 14 - June 16, 6pm-8pm via Zoom** and helps parents learn to never argue with teens, prevent/intervene in alcohol or drug use, improve school attendance and performance, and explore solutions for media issues. The program uses visual metaphors to teach social, emotional, and leadership principles with a multisensory approach for every learning type. Contact Patsy Bolden at **pbolden@ccswoh.org / 513-867-7072** for more information. (Syllabus fee $10.61 for out-of-county residents)

title: Understanding Decoding: Reading Skills Resources for Parents
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: What does decoding mean? A simple definition for decoding is recognizing letter sounds or patterns and blending them together to translate a written word into speech. Decoding is a foundational reading skill (phonics) that must be developed to begin successful reading with fluency. This process begins with students recognizing their letters and sounds then blending the sounds to speak the word, i.e., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ becomes cat.Here is an example of what happens when a student decodes a word:Recognizing letters and letter patterns (like b, sh, igh)Knowing the sounds they makeBlending those sounds together to read a wordActivities: Reading Rockets is a reputable research-based website for all things reading; and below are age-specific resources for decoding activities.Kindergarten: https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101Kindergartener phonics and decoding activitiesFirst Grade:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-first-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activitiesSecond Grade:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-second-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activitiesThird Grade:Here is a video showing how a 3rd grade student uses syllables to decode longer words more easily.

summary:
**Decoding** is the foundational reading skill of recognizing letter sounds and blending them together to read words (e.g., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ = cat). Reading Rockets provides age-specific activities for parents to support decoding practice:
- **Kindergarten**: [Phonics and decoding activities](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101)
- **First Grade**: [Phonics and decoding activities](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-first-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activities)
- **Second Grade**: [Phonics and decoding activities](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-second-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activities)
- **Third Grade**: Video showing how students use syllables to decode longer words

title: LIFES Mentorship Program at Bogan Elementary
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: If you have questions about the program, please reach out to Mrs. Crowder for more information.

summary: The **LIFES Mentorship Program** pairs 1-2 Miami University students with 3-6 elementary students (grades 3rd-5th) for weekly enrichment activities during lunch/recess. The program focuses on building meaningful relationships, fostering personal growth, and supporting academic and leadership development through activities, games, team-building, and conversations. Benefits include trusted mentorship, positive role models, confidence in communication, strong peer friendships, and enhanced academic and life skills. **Contact Mrs. Crowder for more information.**
